summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (69/44)

data.turoyo: Ono ste gəmwaʕadnanxu, iḏa kan d moṭenoli ḥḏo, d obitu waʕd ʕam aloho, noše d l omər: "Lu ḥakəm kətle abro, walla gmoṭeno ḥḏo, walakən d lo yomituli, lə ggowanno ono."

summary: example for sense 2 in Part. Pass. (Jan 4.I/312)

data.turoyo: Bu darbo, u gawro mwaʕdo we, ʕal asas harke gədmoyəd iqame xayifo.
data.translation: On the way, her husband had been promised that here he would quickly get residence.

rationale: First Detransitive recipient sense 2, contrasted with inherited appointed-time sense 1; separate we remains a copula. Jan translation is machine-generated.

summary: Promisees occur as suffixes, ʕam/aʕm- phrases, bare nouns including aloho and the two servants, or remain implicit. The l-marked lu kurrəko at 24/34 is the agent, not the promise recipient.
Infectum can perform the promise in the speech situation (26/167; 69/44; Talay 2/11). Preterit-wa recalls a prior obligation; an unmarked Preterit in 69/163 can also be anterior in context.

Detransitive Part. Pass. at 69/522 is the existing appointed-hour state, not a new quotation or morphological discovery. Do not treat all promises about marriage as betrothal: the direct person theme distinguishes 1b.
The cognate u waʕd d ... mwaʕadli at 29/408 names a promise and its making; it does not by itself establish an idiom or a light-verb construction. No new idiom is supported.

Round 2 only. Jan English is project machine translation, retained verbatim in selected excerpts; semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo. Round-1 proposals are retained as the baseline and are not repeated in this JSON.
Ordinary promises about political support, a frontier and abstention remain II.1. English had promised does not establish Preterit-wa when the Turoyo lacks -wa.
Jan 4.I/312 has a masculine recipient as subject of mwaʕdo we, followed by promised content. The separate copula does not create a Preterit-wa verb.
Round-1 active 1b marital pledging and 2 obligating the hearer remain in force; none of these Jan active clauses supplies a direct woman theme or hearer-controlled injunction.

At 26/201 does -ləx encode the woman being pledged, or the promisee with omitted propositional content? Keep this ambiguous token under ordinary 1 until confirmed; 1b rests on explicit person themes elsewhere.

Is the performative at 26/248 understood specifically as marital pledging or as ceding an existing marriage claim? The proposed gloss stays within that context, without introducing a broad hand-over sense.
Confirm that h in Talay 2/11 Komwahadno represents ʕ in wʕd, and whether ʕam Aloho denotes counterpart or witness. Preserve the transcription verbatim.
Does 69/167 support a conventional obligating construction beyond this one attestation? The control contrast is clear, but distribution remains to be checked.
Does the recipient Part. Pass. in Jan 4.I/312 conventionally mean having received a promise, or being under an appointment/commitment? Residence content strongly supports the former here.
Correct 'hatte ihn das Versprechen gegeben' to 'hatte ihm das Versprechen gegeben'
rationale: German 'jemandem das Versprechen geben' requires the dative recipient 'ihm'. The supplied translation at 52/34 has 'er hatte ihm das Versprechen gegeben'.

summary: Threats, vows to God, self-directed vows with ʕal ruḥ-, and mutual marriage commitments retain the ordinary commitment meaning. An adverse promised act alone does not create a threat sense.
